subject: Isobar - chewing a paw
body:

subject: Re: Isobar - chewing a paw

facts.plan: vet volunteers will review; circle back tomorrow morning; watch for pain/appetite changes

body:
Hi Farah!

Thank you so much for flagging this. Paw-chewing is SO common, and the fact that she's still eating and playing normally is a really good sign!

Here's the plan: I'm passing your note to our vet volunteers so they can review it, and I'll circle back with you tomorrow morning with their thoughts on monitoring and next steps.

In the meantime, just keep an eye out for any signs of pain (limping, flinching when you touch the paw, whimpering) or changes in her appetite. If you notice either of those, reply here right away!

You're doing great with her (way more observant than I'd be, honestly).

Dana

facts.note: flags for the doctor; small schedule-shift ask (15 minutes)

body:
Hi there,

Thank you so much for sending everything over on Isobar! No worries at all about the thin records. That's pretty common with shelter pulls, and the intake details (DHPP, Bordetella, deworming, and flea treatment) are really helpful.

I've flagged the paw-chewing concern for the doctor so she can take a good look during his visit. Since he's a young pup with only one round of DHPP on file, we'll likely ask that he stay in your arms or the carrier in the lobby until he's further along in his series. Just our standard puppy protocol!

One small ask: would it be possible to shift his appointment 15 minutes later? It would help us out with the doctor's schedule that day. If not, no worries!

Looking forward to meeting Isobar.

Noel, Crestview Team

subject: Struggling with Drumlin — I'm so sorry

facts.reason: resident dog isn't coping with a second dog

body:
Hi all,

I've been putting off writing this for a few days, and honestly I feel awful about it. Drumlin is the sweetest boy!! He's started doing this little happy wiggle every morning when I come downstairs, and he's figured out exactly which cupboard the treats live in. But our resident dog just isn't coping with having a second dog in the house. She's stopped eating properly, hides upstairs most of the day, and goes stiff whenever Drumlin comes near her, even though he's only ever polite with her.

I really thought she'd settle in time, and I hate feeling like I'm letting him down. What should I do next? I'm happy to keep him until you find another foster, and I'll write up everything I've learned about him so his next home has a head start!!

So sorry,
Anouk

facts.pointer: redirect to animal control / lost-pet groups

body:
Hi Keiko!

Thank you SO much for stopping to help him. Sandy, friendly, and a little scared sounds like a pup who's very much missed by someone!

We're a small foster-based rescue, so we can't take in strays directly (I wish I could scoop them all up, trust me). Your best first step is your local animal control. They're the official place owners check, and they can scan him for a microchip. Most vet offices will scan for free too!

It's also worth posting a photo and where you found him (near the old bus shelter on Maple) to local lost-pet groups. Those find owners FAST.

Fingers crossed he's home by tonight!

Dana

body:

subject: Photos of Virga
body:
Hi all,

Attached is a backyard set of Virga, about a dozen shots. Natural light, mostly from late afternoon, so there should be a few good ones for her listing. Pick whatever works and I'll retake anything that doesn't.

Fair warning for whoever adopts her: Virga does zoomies at 8pm sharp. Not 7:55, not 8:10. I've started checking the clock and clearing the patio chairs out of her racetrack by quarter to. Three laps of the yard, one victory lap, then she flops down like nothing happened. A couple of the blurrier shots are from that, if you want an action photo.

If anyone else needs help with photos for their fosters, I'm happy to swing by.

Yolanda

subject: Bio for Virga
body:

Home recommendation: no cats please. She's sweet as anything with people, but she gets very interested in anything small that moves.

Behavioral note for the listing: those 8pm zoomies are a feature, not a bug. If you let her run them out, she's settled and snoozing by 8:15 like clockwork. Adopters with a fenced yard or a hallway they don't mind sacrificing for ten minutes will do great. Happy to chat with anyone who applies about her evening routine.

Also, if anyone else needs bio help or a second set of eyes on a questionnaire this week, send it my way.

Yolanda
